newsitem.title: GERMANY: Most Bonn 1996 privatisations seen delayed - SPD.
newsitem.headline: Most Bonn 1996 privatisations seen delayed - SPD.

text.p: The German government is likely to realise only a small fraction of the nine billion marks ($5.9 billion) in privatisation revenues seen in its 1996 budget, a key opposition parliamentarian said on Wednesday.
Social Democrat (SPD) budget spokesman Karl Diller said delays in most of the planned sales would add to Finance Minister Theo Waigel's troubles in keeping the budget deficit below 70 billion marks.

Diller distributed a Finance Ministry report showing that planned deals such as the sale of government interests in Lufthansa AG, Postbank AG and Autobahn Tank & Rast AG were unlikely to be completed this year.
Only the 89 million mark sale of Neckar AG had already been completed, and one public housing project might be sold, the report said.
"The current budget is running headlong between the millstones of tens of billions of marks in unrealised tax and privatisation revenues, and above-plan costs for unemployment," Diller said.
"(Finance Minister Theo) Waigel's contention that he can limit this year's deficit to 70 billion marks becomes less believable by the day."

This year's budget plan included four billion marks in federal revenues from the Frankfurter Siedlungsgesellschaft mbH that are unlikely to come in because the government has not reached agreement with state and local authorities that also hold shares, Diller said.

The sale of part of Postbank was also supposed to bring in 3.1 billion marks, but it will only be possible if Postbank and Deutsche Post AG iron out outstanding differences by early November, and then reach further agreements with partners by the end of the year.

The Lufthansa sale, budgeted at 1.7 billion marks, will require legislation to ensure that the majority of shares remain in German hands, a proposal that is being reviewed by European Union authorities.
-- Terence Gallagher, Bonn newsroom, 49 228 26097150 ($ = 1.527 German Marks)
